claim.pdf_says: The paragraph "Alphabet-name-1 is used for code-set conversion of each data item described with usage display in the selected record description entry. ..." and the following "NOTE    There is no conversion of data items described with other usages unless a FORMAT clause applies." are printed indented to the body margin of numbered General rule 4) (which begins on page 414), i.e. they are continuation paragraphs of rule 4); numbered rule "5) If a FORMAT clause is also specified for the file, ..." resumes at the outer margin.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md Page 415 slice, lines 6 and 8: "Alphabet-name-1 is used for code-set conversion of each data item described with usage display in the selected record description entry. ..." and "NOTE    There is no conversion of data items described with other usages unless a FORMAT clause applies." are both flush at column 0, the same level as the numbered rules themselves. Likewise the two em-dash bullets belonging to rule 5) ("— formatting first, then code-set conversion during output operations;" / "— code-set conversion first, then formatting during input operations.") are at column 0, while a)/b) under rule 6) on the same page ARE indented three spaces.
claim.why_it_matters: Losing the indentation detaches two normative continuation paragraphs and a NOTE from CODE-SET General rule 4), so a reader cannot tell whether 'Alphabet-name-1 is used for code-set conversion...' is part of rule 4 or a free-standing rule; the same flattening makes rule 5)'s two-item bullet list render as sibling paragraphs of the numbered rules. The inconsistency is internal to the page (rule 6)'s sub-items are indented, rule 5)'s are not).

verdict.reasoning:
Every factual observation in the claim checks out, but the defect is indentation only -- explicitly a formatting difference, not misplaced content, and it changes no meaning.

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE PDF (300 dpi render of spec_p415.png = printed page 385, plus PyMuPDF line-bbox extraction of the text layer, x-offsets only since the text layer is obfuscated per reference_spec_encoding):
  x0=80.04  ->  numbered rules "5)", "6)", "7)" (outer margin)
  x0=97.5   ->  rule-body wrap column, AND: the page-top continuation of rule 4) (y=90.5-115.8), the "Alphabet-name-1 is used..." paragraph (y=141.1-166.4), the "NOTE There is no conversion..." line (y=191.0), both em-dash bullets under 5) (y=240.3, y=265.6), and the "a)"/"b)" enumerators under 6) (y=316.2, y=354.1)
  x0=115.05 ->  wrapped continuation lines inside a) and b)
So yes: the Alphabet-name-1 paragraph and the NOTE sit at the rule-body margin and are structurally continuation paragraphs of General rule 4). And note the claim's own internal-inconsistency point is confirmed from the other side too -- in the PDF the em-dash bullets under 5) and the a)/b) enumerators under 6) are at the SAME x (97.5), yet the markdown gives a)/b) three spaces and the em-dashes zero.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONTENT DISCREPANCY:
1) Nothing is missing. The page-spanning sentence of rule 4) is correctly rejoined: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 17804 already reads "...If there are no record description entries associated with the file, the record description used for conversion is the description of the identifier or literal specified in the FROM phrase of a WRITE or REWRITE statement specifying the FILE phrase." The PDF's page-top continuation fragment is fully accounted for on the page-414 side -- ordinary page-break furniture, handled correctly.
2) Nothing is out of order and nothing is misattributed. The two paragraphs and the NOTE appear in the markdown between rule 4) and rule 5) (lines 17811, 17813), exactly where the PDF puts them. No rule is renumbered; no sentence migrates from one rule to another. A reader cannot mistake the Alphabet-name-1 paragraph for part of rule 5) -- it textually precedes 5).
3) Rule 5)'s bullet list is unambiguous regardless of indent: 5) ends in a colon ("...the logical order of processing for each data item is:") and the two em-dash items follow immediately before 6). Also, "— " is an em dash, not a markdown list marker, so the items render as plain text at either indent level -- the three spaces would change no rendering, only source alignment.
4) The normative requirement is identical either way. Citing the sentence as "13.18.13.4 GR 4, third paragraph" versus "an unnumbered paragraph between GR 4 and GR 5" changes precision of reference at worst; it changes no compiler-observable semantics of the CODE-SET clause.

HONEST CAVEAT (recorded, but not the claimed defect): the transcription's own house style elsewhere DOES indent continuation paragraphs, NOTEs and em-dash bullets under numbered items by three spaces -- e.g. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 3032-3035, 3048, 4037-4041, 4261, 4273, 4561-4564, 4921, 5152, 5160. So page 415 deviates from the document's own convention and is worth a whitespace cleanup. But that is a cosmetic normalization, severity cosmetic, kind=indentation -- not kind=misplaced-content and not severity=structural. Under the rejection criteria ("the difference is only page-break furniture, line wrapping, hyphenation, or formatting" / "the difference does not change meaning") this claim is rejected.
verdict.corrected_description: REJECTED as filed. The claim's observations are factually accurate -- in the PDF (printed p. 385) the "Alphabet-name-1 is used..." paragraph, the following NOTE, and both em-dash bullets under rule 5) all sit at x0=97.5, the rule-body margin, while numbered rules 5)/6)/7) sit at x0=80.0; and in specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 17811/17813/17817/17819 those four items are at column 0 while a)/b) at lines 17823/17825 carry three spaces. But this is a leading-whitespace difference only. No text is missing (rule 4)'s page-spanning sentence is correctly rejoined at line 17804), no text is reordered, no sentence is attributed to the wrong numbered rule, and the em-dash items remain bound to rule 5) by its terminal colon and by position before 6). Reclassify, if tracked at all, as kind=indentation / severity=cosmetic: "page 415 flattens rule 4)'s two continuation paragraphs, its NOTE, and rule 5)'s two em-dash items to column 0, deviating from the transcription's own three-space convention (cf. lines 3048, 4261, 4921, 5152) and from the uniform x0=97.5 indent the PDF gives all of them -- including the a)/b) items the markdown does indent." No normative content or meaning is affected.
